subject: Materials Science
title: Carbon Nanofibers in Composites
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Carbon Nanofibers in Composites.

hook.text: Add 2% carbon nanofibers to a polymer and its strength doubles — reinforcement at the molecular level.

buildup.text: Carbon nanofibers (CNFs) are 50–200 nm diameter cylinders — larger than CNTs but much cheaper to produce.

discovery.text: Vapor-grown CNFs form in a catalytic CVD process — iron nanoparticles seed the growth of aligned fiber forests.

twist.text: Dispersion is the challenge — CNFs clump via van der Waals forces, creating weak spots instead of strength.

climax.text: Surface-treated CNFs in polymers make lighter, stronger car parts, wind turbine blades, and sports gear.

punchline.text: Tiny fibers in plastic — invisible reinforcement, stronger and lighter.

quiz.question: What is the main processing challenge with carbon nanofibers?
options: They are too fragile to survive mixing
They tend to clump together due to van der Waals forces, requiring surface treatment
They react chemically with all polymer matrices
